title: Arrays: input, sum, search, min/max
overview: Arrays store many values under one name, indexed from 0. This module reads arrays and prints them back, then uses one loop over the array to sum, average, search, replace values and find the minimum or maximum with its position. These single-pass patterns come up in almost every later problem.

concepts.explain: `int a[n];` holds `n` ints, from `a[0]` to `a[n-1]`. Read and print them with a `for` loop.
concepts.snippet: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) scanf("%d", &a[i]);

concepts.explain: Start `sum = 0` and add each element. Use `long long` when the total can go past about 2×10^9.
`(double) sum / n` converts to `double` before dividing. Otherwise the division is integer division and the fraction is lost.
Scan from the left and `break` at the first match. Start `pos = -1` to mean 'not found'.
Start from `a[0]` (or `INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN`) and update whenever you see a smaller or bigger value. Using strict `<` keeps the first position when values tie.
Arrays in C start at 0, but some tasks ask for positions starting at 1. Add 1 only when printing.

files.title: Read and print 5 values
files.what: Reads exactly five integers into `a[5]` and prints them back on one line.
steps: Loop again and print `a[i]` followed by a space.
files.output_note: The same five numbers come back, each followed by a space.

check.q: What is the index of the last element of `int a[5]`?

files.title: Sum and average
files.what: Reads n values, prints their sum, then prints the average as a `double`.
steps: Compute `avg = (double) sum / n` so the division keeps the fraction.
files.output_note: The sum is `105`, and 105 / 4 = `26.250000` (`%lf` shows 6 decimals).

check.q: What would `avg` be without the `(double)` cast?
check.a: 26.000000. Integer division throws away the .25 before the result is stored.

files.title: Minimum and maximum of an array
files.what: Finds the smallest and largest elements in one pass, starting from `INT_MAX` and `INT_MIN`.
steps: `min = INT_MAX` and `max = INT_MIN` (from `<limits.h>`), so the first element always replaces them.
For each `a[i]`: if it is smaller than `min`, update `min`; if it is bigger than `max`, update `max`.

check.a: If every element were positive, a starting value of 0 would never be replaced, and the answer would be wrong.

files.title: A. Summation (absolute sum)
files.what: Adds up all the numbers and prints the absolute value of the total, using `long long` and `llabs`.
steps: Read each value into a `long long x` and add it to `sum`. The array does not need to be stored.
files.output_note: -1 + 2 - 3 = -2, and its absolute value is `2`, which matches the task's sample.

check.a: `abs` works on `int`, so a large `long long` sum would be cut off. `llabs` works on `long long`.

files.title: B. Searching (first position)
files.what: Searches for `x` from left to right and prints the index of its first occurrence, or -1 if it is missing.
steps: At the first `a[i] == x`, set `pos = i` and `break`.
files.output_note: 2 appears at indexes 0 and 2. The `break` stops at the first one, so the output is `0`.

check.a: `2`, the last matching index, which is not what the task asks for.

files.title: C. Replacement
files.what: Replaces each positive number with 1 and each negative number with 2, leaves zeros alone, and prints the array without a trailing space.
steps: For each element: if it is `> 0`, set it to 1; else if it is `< 0`, set it to 2.
Print the first element on its own, then print `" %d"` for each of the rest, so there is no trailing space.
files.output_note: The output is `1 2 0 1 1`, the same as the task's sample.

check.q: Why print `" %d"` for every element after the first?
check.a: The space comes before each number, so there is never an extra space at the end of the line.

files.title: D. Positions in array

problem.name: Codeforces group - D. Positions in array

files.what: Prints `A[i] = x` for every element that is 10 or less.
files.output_note: There are three lines, for indexes 0, 1 and 3. 100 and 30 are skipped.

check.q: Would a negative value like -7 be printed?

files.title: E. Lowest Number and its position
files.what: Finds the minimum value and the 1-based position of its first occurrence.
steps: For `i` from 1, if `a[i] < min_val`, update both. The strict `<` keeps the first position when values tie.
files.output_note: The minimum 2 appears at positions 3 and 5 (counting from 1). The first is kept, so the output is `2 3`.

check.q: What changes if you use `<=` instead of `<`?
check.a: The last occurrence would be reported, giving `2 5`.

recap: Arrays run from index 0 to n-1, so loop with `i < n`.
Accumulate into `long long` when the total can be large.
Cast to `double` before dividing to get a real average.
Search with `pos = -1` and `break` at the first match.
Use strict `<` to keep the first minimum; add 1 only when printing 1-based positions.

check_yourself.q: An array has n = 10^5 values, each up to 10^9. What type should `sum` be?
check_yourself.a: `long long`, because the total can reach 10^14.

check_yourself.q: How do you print an array space-separated without a trailing space?
check_yourself.a: Print the first element alone, then print `" %d"` for each of the others.

check_yourself.q: What does `pos` stay at if the value is never found?
What is `7 / 2` in C, and what is `(double) 7 / 2`?
